subject: physiology
title: The Ovarian Cycle, Folliculogenesis, and the LH Surge

steps.tx: The normal female reproductive cycle operates under periodic hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone pulses that drive anterior pituitary gonadotropin secretion. Over an average twenty-eight-day duration, rhythmic follicular maturation, ovulation, and luteal transformation define the **ovarian cycle**, establishing coordinate hormonal fluctuations that simultaneously direct uterine endometrial development and prepare maternal tissues for potential pregnancy.
steps.say: The ovarian cycle coordinates follicular growth, ovulation, and luteal transformation under pulsatile pituitary gonadotropin drive.

steps.tx: During the initial twelve to fourteen days of the ovarian cycle, follicle-stimulating hormone stimulates the recruitment and growth of a cohort of antral follicles. Under progressive gonadotropin support, granulosa cells proliferate and secrete follicular fluid, constituting the **follicular phase** of the cycle where a single dominant Graafian follicle emerges while subordinate follicles undergo apoptotic atresia.
steps.say: FSH drives granulosa cell proliferation and fluid accumulation during the follicular phase, selecting a single dominant follicle.

steps.tx: As the dominant follicle enlarges, its proliferating granulosa layer secretes progressively mounting concentrations of estradiol. When sustained circulating estradiol concentrations exceed two hundred picograms per milliliter for more than thirty-six hours, pituitary feedback paradoxically switches from negative to positive, triggering the explosive **LH surge** that initiates resumption of oocyte meiosis.
steps.say: High sustained estradiol levels trigger positive pituitary feedback, producing the massive LH surge that drives ovulation.

steps.tx: Approximately thirty-four to thirty-six hours following the onset of the luteinizing hormone surge, follicular rupture expels the cumulus-oocyte complex into the peritoneal cavity. This mechanical and enzymatic extrusion of the mature secondary oocyte arrested in metaphase two represents **ovulation**, facilitated by prostaglandin-mediated local vasodilation and collagenase digestion of the follicular apex.
steps.say: Ovulation expels the mature secondary oocyte thirty-six hours after the LH surge begins, aided by collagenase enzymes.

Ruptured follicle collapses and hemorrhages into antral cavity

steps.tx: Following follicular rupture, the collapsed follicle wall undergoes extensive vascularization and luteinization of its granulosa and theca cells under the trophic support of luteinizing hormone. The resulting endocrine gland is the **corpus luteum**, which rapidly assumes intense steroidogenic output to dominate the second half of the ovarian cycle.
steps.say: The ruptured follicle transforms into the vascularized corpus luteum, which secretes abundant progesterone and estrogen.

vis.caption: Corpus luteum formation after ovulation under hCG signalling. [Credit: StewardMD]
vis.alt: Corpus luteum formation after ovulation under hCG signalling.

steps.tx: Granulosa lutein cells within the corpus luteum synthesize and release large quantities of progesterone, supported by modest amounts of estradiol and inhibin A. Circulating **progesterone** converts estrogen-primed proliferative endometrium into a tortuous, glycogen-rich secretory mucosa, while simultaneously exerting potent negative feedback on hypothalamic gonadotropin-releasing hormone release to suppress new follicular recruitment.
steps.say: Progesterone from granulosa lutein cells turns the endometrium secretory while suppressing new follicular development.

steps.tx: If fertilisation and blastocyst implantation fail to occur, the absence of chorionic gonadotropin leads to autonomous regression of the corpus luteum approximately ten to twelve days after ovulation. As steroidogenesis terminates, the gland involutes into a fibrous avascular scar termed the **corpus albicans**, removing negative feedback inhibition on pituitary gonadotropin release.
steps.say: Without pregnancy, the corpus luteum regresses into a fibrous corpus albicans, allowing FSH levels to rise again.

left.title: Luteal Involution (No Pregnancy)
points: Corpus luteum lifespan is fixed at twelve to fourteen days
Local endothelin-1 and PGF2-alpha promote luteolysis
Involutes into white fibrous connective tissue corpus albicans

right.title: Luteal Rescue (Pregnancy)
points: hCG binds LH receptors to maintain corpus luteum viability
High progesterone output maintained through first trimester
Placental steroidogenesis assumes maintenance by eight to ten weeks

steps.tx: The abrupt withdrawal of circulating estrogen and progesterone resulting from luteal regression triggers intense spiral arteriolar vasospasm within the superficial stratum functionale of the uterine endometrium. Ischemia, tissue necrosis, and leukocyte infiltration culminate in shedding of the necrotic mucosa, marking the **menstrual phase** that designates day one of the concurrent endometrial cycle.
steps.say: Steroid withdrawal causes spiral artery vasospasm and ischemic shedding of the functionalis layer during menstruation.
